_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); machinery and engines signals

pit_profile.why: 'Caterpillar is the world’s leading manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, diesel and natural gas engines, industrial gas turbines and diesel-electric locomotives' (FY2017 10-K, Item 1); 'Caterpillar products and product support services are sold worldwide into a variety of highly competitive markets'; 'The demand for our products and services tends to be cyclical and can be significantly reduced in periods of economic weakness characterized by lower levels of government and business investment, lower levels of business confidence, lower corporate earnings, high real interest rates, lower credit activity or tighter credit conditions, perceived or actual industry overcapacity, higher unemployment and lower consumer spending.', 'The energy, transportation and mining industries are major users of our products, including the coal, iron ore, gold, copper, oil and natural gas industries.' and 'Changes in environmental and climate change laws or regulations, including laws relating to greenhouse gas emissions, could lead to new or additional investment in product designs and could increase environmental compliance expenditures.' (Item 1A): the 10-K calls the demand for its own products cyclical (BKR's 'Our business is cyclical'), so CYCLICAL from the FY2010 10-K; ENERGY_TRANSITION is live from 2015-12-12 but scoped to oil, gas and coal reserves and refining, which a maker of construction and mining equipment, engines and turbines does not hold, so the climate-change wording stays here

classification.quality_note: 'Caterpillar is the world’s leading manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, diesel and natural gas engines, industrial gas turbines and diesel-electric locomotives' (FY2017 10-K, Item 1); 'Caterpillar products and product support services are sold worldwide into a variety of highly competitive markets'; 'The demand for our products and services tends to be cyclical and can be significantly reduced in periods of economic weakness characterized by lower levels of government and business investment, lower levels of business confidence, lower corporate earnings, high real interest rates, lower credit activity or tighter credit conditions, perceived or actual industry overcapacity, higher unemployment and lower consumer spending.', 'The energy, transportation and mining industries are major users of our products, including the coal, iron ore, gold, copper, oil and natural gas industries.' and 'Changes in environmental and climate change laws or regulations, including laws relating to greenhouse gas emissions, could lead to new or additional investment in product designs and could increase environmental compliance expenditures.' (Item 1A): the 10-K calls the demand for its own products cyclical (BKR's 'Our business is cyclical'), so CYCLICAL from the FY2010 10-K; ENERGY_TRANSITION is live from 2015-12-12 but scoped to oil, gas and coal reserves and refining, which a maker of construction and mining equipment, engines and turbines does not hold, so the climate-change wording stays here. cyclical (obsolescence risk 2/5); price cheap; Ratio B 0.62x; +4% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +1.82; conservative 2yr +84%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -61.5%/yr (worst year FY08-FY17, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +24.2%/yr (Q2 sales and revenues + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +24.2%/yr (FY08-FY17 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +43.4%/yr (best 2-yr run FY08-FY17); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: CAT (retrospective, 2018-07-31) ◉ BUY — Ratio B 0.62x (86.1% downside to Bear $20 / +139.2% upside to Bull $344) | Adj composite 3.50 vs market 1.68: gap +1.82 [UNDERVALUED] | +4% above the EPP floor $138 (12x FY18E $11.50) | Conservative 2-yr case: +84.1% total (+42.1%/yr) | At 12.5x FY18E the 15% hurdle price $190 sits at or below the BASE case; Machinery sales +28.1% in Q2 2018, forward revenues +23.7% (no FY18 sales and revenues guide in numbers, Q2 2018 growth); ENERGY_TRANSITION is live from 2015-12-12 but scoped to oil, gas and coal reserves and refining; no theme in scope has dated evidence.
